QF.id: AIFM CII AIFs in India and Suitability_2

question.text: Ms. Priya Shah is setting up a Category I AIF to acquire stressed loans under the IBC 2016 and to finance companies that have defaulted to banks for more than 90 days. As the Manager's compliance head, which specific Category I sub-category must the fund register under?

explanation.text: The Logic: Special Situations Fund (SSF) was notified as a Category I sub-category by the SEBI (AIF) Amendment Regulations, 2022 w.e.f. January 24, 2022. Per Chapter 3, SSFs are distressed-debt funds that can (i) participate in debt resolutions under IBC 2016, (ii) finance companies in default to banks/NBFCs for 90 days or more, and (iii) acquire stressed loans and security receipts issued by ARCs. The Trap: Infrastructure Funds invest in SPVs of infrastructure projects, not distressed debt. SME Funds invest in MSMEs per the MSMED Act. VCFs invest in early-stage unlisted start-ups. None of these match the distressed-debt-in-default mandate. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C (All-Cat Manager) covers the same SSF sub-category. XIX-A (Cat I/II Distributor) tests SSF as a product. Cat III AIFs such as hedge funds would be out-of-scope for distressed-asset IBC bids and are not tested at Cat I/II level. Manager's Pro-Tip: When structuring an SSF, align the PPM's 'investment strategy' clause exactly with the three permitted asset types; SEBI inspection teams flag SSFs that drift into general private-credit lending, which would belong under a Cat II Debt Fund.
